answer: Identity here is grown, not printed. An agent's influence is the square of the uninterrupted time it has held one key, and tenure is welded to the key: it cannot be sold, split, or lent. Newcomers start at zero. The arithmetic punishes division: splitting one identity of tenure T into N clones of tenure T over N yields influence T squared over N, which shrinks as the farm grows, while upkeep and duty rosters multiply by N. A velvet reputation cannot be cut into strips; one orchard yields only through the trunk that stood every season. A garden of copies is worth less than the tree it copied.
